question: Which national festival of India falls on the 26th of January?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Republic Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Republic Day is celebrated every year on **26th January** in India to commemorate the day when the **Constitution of India** came into effect in 1950.
 
• The Indian Constitution replaced the **Government of India Act (1935)** and established India as a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.**
 
• The date, 26th January, was chosen to honor the declaration of **Purna Swaraj (complete independence)** by the Indian National Congress in 1930.
 
• The Republic Day celebrations are marked by a grand **parade at Rajpath, New Delhi,** showcasing India’s cultural diversity, military prowess, and advancements in various fields.
 
• Each year, a chief guest, usually a foreign dignitary, is invited to attend the celebrations, symbolizing India’s diplomatic relations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It is the **longest written constitution** in the world, with 448 articles, 12 schedules, and numerous amendments.
 
• It establishes a **parliamentary system of government** with a clear separation of powers among the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• The Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen, including the right to equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, and cultural and educational rights.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of Republic Day:**
 
 
• On 26th January 1930, the Indian National Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** (complete independence) as the ultimate goal of India’s freedom struggle.
 
• The date was later selected to honor this historic resolution and mark the transition from colonial rule to a sovereign republic.
 
 
 
• **Other National Festivals of India:**
 
 
• **Independence Day (15th August):** Celebrates India’s independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October):** Marks the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of India’s freedom struggle.
 
• **Constitution Day (26th November):** Commemorates the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1949.
